label: Thomas Aquinas, Summa theologiae I q.5 a.1 co: A thing is desirable in a given perfection exactly…
locator: I q.5 a.1 co.: Manifestum est autem quod unumquodque est appetibile secundum quod est perfectum: nam omnia appetunt suam perfectionem
interpretation: Second step: each thing is desirable according as it is perfect. 'Secundum quod' is read as a per-perfection biconditional, the same reading the conclusion's 'intantum ... inquantum' receives in STMT-GOODNESS-IS-ACTUALITY. The stated reason, that all things desire their own perfection, supports only the direction from perfect to desirable; the converse (nothing is desirable except as perfect) rests on the 'secundum quod' reading, not on the reason. Perfect here is perfection in the respect at issue (DISAMB-PERFECT-IN-A-RESPECT-OR-UNIVERSALLY).
